concept.name: Seasonal ARIMA
concept.definition: A multiplicative extension of the ARIMA model that adds seasonal autoregressive, seasonal differencing, and seasonal moving-average terms at the seasonal period s, written SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)_s, to model series with stable repeating periodic patterns.
concept.intuition: Monthly sales or quarterly earnings resemble not only the adjacent period but the same period a year ago, so the model regresses on lags spaced by the season length as well as on short lags.
concept.mechanics: In addition to the non-seasonal operators phi(B), theta(B) and differencing (1-B)^d, the model includes seasonal polynomials Phi(B^s), Theta(B^s) and seasonal differencing (1-B^s)^D, usually combined multiplicatively. Identification examines ACF spikes at the seasonal lags s, 2s, ... alongside the short lags.
concept.formula: phi(B) Phi(B^s) (1-B)^d (1-B^s)^D X_t = theta(B) Theta(B^s) A_t, where s is the seasonal period and (P,D,Q) the seasonal AR, differencing, and MA orders.
concept.failure_modes: The parameter count grows quickly with seasonal terms, inviting overfitting on short samples; several full seasonal cycles are needed for identification. If the seasonal pattern itself shifts (calendar changes, regime change), the fixed-period terms misfit.
concept.misconceptions: That seasonal ARIMA discovers arbitrary periodicities: s must be specified a priori from the data frequency, and the model assumes the seasonal period and shape are stable over the sample.
concept.example: Monthly airline passengers spike every December; SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)_12 differences once and seasonally, then models residuals with both a one-month and a twelve-month moving-average term.

citations.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 6.4.4.5 Box-Jenkins Models
